case.title: Fabricated points stepped 44.5 m apart in a line still catch the middle one

submissions.open_text: Farmer irrigates vegetables and also drinks from the stream after storms.
Retired clerk has an indoor tap and rarely experiences shortages.
Student hostel residents queue at a shared standpipe before lectures.

case.why: Adversarial: a fabricator nudges each fake GPS fix about 44.5 m (0.0004 deg latitude) along a line, hoping no tight cluster forms. a and c are each about 44.5 m from t, but about 89 m from each other. The rule counts each submission's own neighbours. So t, the middle point, has 2 neighbours within 50 m and must fire, while a and c each have only 1 and would not. An implementation that would miss t: one that needs the neighbours to be mutually within 50 m (a clique), or measures from the day's first point or the centroid. Times are two hours apart, so there is no burst. Each text is distinct and every point is inside Kondele.
